cd $PWD; cat > /tmp/body.md <<'EOF'
Fixes #35.

## What changes

When a prompt settles, `ThreadConversation` now looks at the **stop reason** of the last assistant message (`Thread.answerText()` reports it). Before, it only checked whether the final text was empty.

- **`length` with no tool call** (the agent loop ended, but the model didn't choose to stop): pi sends a continuation prompt with tools still available. It reads: *"Your last response hit the output token limit (max_tokens) before you finished. Continue where you left off; keep reasoning shorter and act with tools."* A warning is logged that names `model_max_tokens`.
- **Retry limit:** up to 3 cut-offs in a row. If a continuation run executed tools before it was cut off again, the count resets. pi detects this by finding a tool result between the submission's input entry and its answer.
- **Still `length` after that:** pi posts an error comment instead of a summary prompt. The comment says the responses hit the output token limit N times in a row, suggests raising `model_max_tokens` (or using a model with a larger output limit), and includes the last partial text. A warning is logged too.
- **`length` with partial text:** the text is posted with a note that it was cut off and pi is continuing, and then pi continues.
- **Timeout:** no continuation is sent once the run's `timeout` is reached or has passed. The result reports the timeout and includes any partial text.
- **Real empty `stop`:** there is still exactly one summary re-prompt, but `SUMMARY_PROMPT` is now neutral. It asks what was done and which files changed, what is left, and any errors. It no longer claims the work is complete.
- **Dedup across runs:** continuations use stable request IDs (`<key>-continue-<n>`, alongside `<key>-summary`), so a re-run gets the existing submissions back instead of sending new ones. Partial texts are posted under their own `answer-<entryId>` keys and recorded in `this.posted`, so they aren't posted twice.

### Tools in the summary re-prompt

**Tools are allowed** there now. An empty `stop` doesn't mean the work is finished; the model may just have stopped early. The old "Do NOT call any tools" told it the job was over, and (as in #33) gave it no way to finish. The new prompt lets it continue with tools if something it was asked to do is still unfinished, but it must still end its turn with a text reply. If that reply is empty too, the existing "failed after two attempts" error is reported. The neutral prompt also makes sense on its own. We couldn't actually prevent tool calls before either: the old prompt only asked the model not to make them.

## Open questions: decisions

- **Retry limit:** 3 in a row, *and* bounded by the remaining `timeout`. Responses that use tools in between reset the count.
- **Default `model_max_tokens`:** left at 16384 and documented instead. The maximum is per model and per provider, so a higher default would fail on models with smaller caps. The README row for `model_max_tokens` now explains what happens when a response hits the limit.

## Tests (`src/run.test.ts`, faux model)

- one `length` stop, then a tool call, then a normal finish: one continuation, no summary prompt, normal reply posted
- `length` stops past the limit: 4 model calls, cut-off error comment, no "completed your work" or summary prompt
- tool use between cut-offs resets the count
- `length` with partial text: partial posted with the cut-off note, then the continuation's reply
- partial text included in the give-up comment
- a later run sends no continuation again and doesn't re-post the partial text
- the timeout stops continuations
- an empty `stop`: one neutral summary prompt

`npm run check` passes: typecheck, lint, coverage and analyze (knip/jscpd).
EOF
gh pr create --base main --head fix/35-max-tokens-continuation --title "fix: continue responses cut off by max_tokens; neutral summary prompt" --body-file /tmp/body.md
